title: Monoidal derived inflation and graded cup composition
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site and $G$ a profinite group, in the universes and internal module/action categories of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-size-convention]. Use ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and internal derived tensor over $A$. Trivial inflation induces an exact strong symmetric monoidal functor
$$L:D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A_G(A)),$$
with $L(A[0])=A[0]$, and a canonical derived adjunction $L\dashv R\Gamma_G$. The derived adjunction is the one obtained from the invariant inclusion and equivariant injective resolutions, namely the canonical derived adjunction of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], whose underived inflation/invariants adjunction is that of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation] with the second group trivial. The tensor and unit comparisons are induced by the identity on ordinary coefficient tensors and the unit; the shift comparisons use the usual shifted cochain complexes.

Give $C=R\Gamma_G(A[0])$ its canonical unital derived cup product, namely the lax monoidal structure adjoint to the inverse strong monoidal structure of $L$, followed by the unit multiplication $A\otimes_A^L A\cong A$. Let $\Phi_q:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A_G(A))}(A,A[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)}(A[-q],C)$ be the shifted adjunction bijection. It sends the identity of $A$ to the cup unit. For $x:A\to A[p]$ and $y:A\to A[q]$, the adjoint of $\Phi_p(x)\smile\Phi_q(y)$ is the tensor of the two arrows, using the fixed tensor/shift comparisons. Equivalently, there are signs $t_{p,q}\in\{1,-1\}$ depending only on $p,q$ and those comparisons such that
$$\Phi_p(x)\smile\Phi_q(y)=t_{p,q}\,\Phi_{p+q}\bigl(y[p]\circ x\bigr).$$
The signs are independent of $A,G,x,y$ and equal $1$ when $p=0$ or $q=0$. The order of this formula is part of the assertion. It holds for all $p,q\geq0$, including the zero ring and the trivial group.

proof.text: Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(*_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}})$ and $K=\underline G$. Apply [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction] to the chosen small profinite site. It presents the action category as modules over $p_K^{-1}A$ on the small action topos, identifies $p_K^*$ with trivial inflation, and identifies its ordinary tensor and unit comparisons with the identity on coefficient tensors and on $A$. Apply [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] to these two small ringed sites and [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to $p_K$. This supplies the ordinary unbounded derived tensors and the symmetric strong monoidal structure on $Lp_K^*$. In particular the symmetry is the signed cochain symmetry, rather than an unsigned tensor symmetry.

proof.text: Let $T$ be trivial inflation. The underived adjunction $T\dashv\Gamma_G$ is the invariant-inclusion adjunction of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation], with the second group trivial. Its categories are Grothendieck abelian and $T$ is additive and exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], its derived functor $L=D(T)$ is triangulated, represented termwise, has the usual signed cochain shifts, and sends $A[0]$ to $A[0]$. It is $Lp_K^*$ from step 1: both are the canonical derived functor of the same exact module pullback. The canonical adjunction in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] therefore gives $L\dashv F=R\Gamma_G$. The right derived functor is computed by equivariant injective resolutions on bounded-below objects as in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]; the underived transpose is exactly the invariant inclusion, so this is the specified derived adjunction, with no new choice of its unit or counit. The canonical adjunction shift theorem [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift] applies because these Grothendieck categories admit K-injective resolutions by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective], and gives shift compatibility for the unit and counit.

proof.text:
Write $I=A[0]$ in either category, $\varepsilon:LF\to1$ for the counit, and $m:I\otimes^LI\to I$ for unit multiplication. By [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates], the inverse strong monoidal structure on $L$ gives a lax monoidal structure $(e,\mu)$ on $F$. Its defining transpose is
$$\varepsilon_{U\otimes V}\circ L(\mu_{U,V})=(\varepsilon_U\otimes\varepsilon_V)\circ t_{FU,FV},$$
where $t:L(-\otimes-)\to L(-)\otimes L(-)$ is the inverse tensor comparison. Put $C=FI$ and $M=F(m)\circ\mu_{I,I}$. The lax associativity and unit diagrams give the associativity and unit equations for $(C,M,e)$, using those of $m$. The monoidal unit/counit theorem [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit] ensures these are the tensor and unit comparisons of this actual adjunction. The transpose of $e:I\to FI$ is the unit comparison $LI\to I$, hence the identity under the prescribed identification.

proof.text:
For $S_n=I[-n]$ and $x:I\to I[p]$, put $f=x[-p]:S_p\to I$ in the action category. The shifted adjunction sends $x$ to the adjoint $a:S_p\to FI$ of $f$; shift compatibility in step 2 identifies this with the specified $\Phi_p$. Likewise write $g=y[-q]$ and $b=\Phi_q(y)$. Let $r_{p,q}:S_{p+q}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_p\otimes^LS_q$ be the fixed shifted-unit comparison. The cup product of $a,b$ is $M\circ(a\otimes b)\circ r_{p,q}$. Transpose this map. Naturality of the counit at $m$, the tensor equation of step 3, and naturality of $t$ turn its transpose into
$$m\circ((\varepsilon_I L(a))\otimes(\varepsilon_I L(b)))\circ L(r_{p,q})=m\circ(f\otimes g)\circ r_{p,q}.$$
Here $L(S_n)=S_n$; the pullback tensor/shift compatibility [lem-pur-shifted-tensor-morphism-calculus] identifies $L(r_{p,q})$ with the same fixed comparison in the action category. This proves the tensor-of-arrows assertion before any graded composition is substituted.

proof.text:
We now compute this tensor of arrows without interchanging $f$ and $g$. For any derived object $Z$ define $\kappa_{Z,q}:Z\otimes^LS_q\to Z[-q]$ by extracting the second shift and then applying the shifted right unitor. The natural signed shift comparisons exist on all derived morphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent], not merely on chain maps between chosen resolutions. On the degree-zero unit $I$, $\kappa_{I,q}$ is the left unitor $\lambda_{S_q}:I\otimes^LS_q\to S_q$: their representative formulas are both multiplication of the ring section, since the first-factor degree is zero. These unitor formulas are those of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Bifunctoriality and left-unitor naturality, followed by naturality of $\kappa$ at $f:S_p\to I$, give
$$m(f\otimes g)=g\lambda_{S_q}(f\otimes1)=g\kappa_{I,q}(f\otimes1)=g f[-q]\kappa_{S_p,q}.$$
This is a three-equality calculation with arbitrary derived arrows; in particular it does not assume that a map from the unit in the action category is represented by an ordinary chain map.

source.place: Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules items shift-tensor and flip-tensor-product; derived extension supplied by the cited shift-descent node

proof.text: Both $\kappa_{S_p,q}r_{p,q}$ and the ordinary identification $S_{p+q}=S_p[-q]$ are maps between the same shifted copies of the regular unit. Compute them on the single nonzero tensor summand $A\otimes_A A$ in total degree $p+q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], extracting the second shift $-q$ on a first factor concentrated in degree $p$ contributes $(-1)^{pq}$; first-shift extraction is unsigned. The fixed comparison $r_{p,q}$ is the shifted-unit identification made from these same signed comparisons. Thus its contribution is also a sign depending only on the integers and the fixed extraction order. Their composite is $t_{p,q}$ times the ordinary shift identification, for $t_{p,q}\in\{1,-1\}$. This computation is valid after localization by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent]. All possible signs here are products of $(-1)^{pq}$: the unit is concentrated in degree zero and only the two shifts are extracted. Hence $t_{p,0}=t_{0,q}=1$. No scalar, group element, or representative of $f,g$ enters this computation.

source.place: Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules item shift-tensor; signed second-factor extraction and the exchange of extraction order

proof.text:
Substitute step 6 into the last equality of step 5 and precompose with $r_{p,q}$. The adjoint of the cup product from step 4 is $t_{p,q}g\circ f[-q]$. Shifting this map by $p+q$ gives exactly $t_{p,q}y[p]\circ x$: indeed $f[-q][p+q]=x$ and $g[p+q]=y[p]$. Additivity of the adjunction bijection therefore gives
$$\Phi_p(x)\smile\Phi_q(y)=t_{p,q}\Phi_{p+q}(y[p]\circ x).$$
No symmetry was used to reverse the arrows. Degree zero has the unsigned unitors, giving both asserted zero-degree normalizations and the identity-to-unit assertion of step 3. Every construction applies to the zero ring: its unit object and all maps are zero, while the integer sign is still the same prescribed sign. For the trivial group, the invariant-inclusion adjunction is the identity adjunction, so the same calculation applies. The argument works for all integer shifts and hence for the required $p,q\geq0$.
